vocabulary.definition: a tendency to expect the best possible outcome or to have a positive outlook on life
vocabulary.example: Despite the challenges, she faced them with optimism and a smile.

vocabulary.definition: a person who habitually sees or anticipates the worst or is inclined to be gloomy
vocabulary.example: He always expects the worst to happen; he's such a pessimist.

vocabulary.definition: excessively or extremely optimistic to an unrealistic degree
vocabulary.example: She was so hyper-optimistic about the project that she ignored all the potential risks.

vocabulary.definition: reaching the lowest possible level or point
vocabulary.example: After losing his job and his savings, he hit rock bottom before finally starting to recover.

vocabulary.definition: to make something seem more positive or less unpleasant than it actually is
vocabulary.example: The manager tried to sugarcoat the bad news about layoffs by emphasizing potential future opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: a stereotype describing an elderly person who is often irritable, cranky, or complains frequently
vocabulary.example: The neighbor is known as the grumpy old man on the street, always yelling at kids playing outside.
